From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Alex — thanks for the quick note and for coordinating next steps. Recap below and a short ask for the steering committee prep.

Demo recap (1 paragraph)
Redwood demonstrated Dedicated + fallback routing to our hosted variants, with predictable throughput guarantees. We showed cost profiles across expected token volumes and the KV cache benefits for repeated prompts. The client-side integration is lightweight (SDK + standard auth).

Immediate asks / gating items
- Procurement: ballpark monthly cost for the committed capacity tiers (we can provide Tier A/B/C estimates).
- Security: preliminary checklist attached (Redwood_Prelim_Security_Checklist.pdf). If you can share your SOC2 report or acceptable substitution, that will speed review.
- Legal: preferred SLAs and indemnity items (we will surface a short standard SOW template).

Steering committee: we can host a 45–60 minute session. Proposed agenda: 1) brief capabilities + perf benchmarks, 2) deployment and network model, 3) security/compliance Q&A, 4) procurement/terms next steps.

Proposed dates (PDT):
- Tue Mar 10, 10:00–11:00
- Wed Mar 11, 14:00–15:00
- Fri Mar 13, 09:00–10:00

Action items for GridLytics
- Confirm who will attend (CTO, Head of MLOps, procurement lead, legal counsel).
- Share any non-negotiable procurement timelines or vendor questionnaire deadlines.

I’ve attached a short security checklist and a draft MAPP (high level) spreadsheet for your internal costing.

Attachments:
- Redwood_Prelim_Security_Checklist.pdf (pdf, 230KB)
- GridLytics_MAPP_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

If those slots look okay I’ll lock one and send calendar invites + a one-page executive summary for the steering committee.

Thanks — Neha

Folks — forwarding the GridLytics thread and attachments. Quick internal plan so we’re aligned before the exec session.

High-level goals for the session:
- Verify that Dedicated meets their throughput SLA and cost expectations for a Q3 rollout.
- Confirm security artifacts we can surface immediately to unblock legal/procurement.
- Identify an initial pilot scope and acceptance criteria (so SOW is narrow).

Suggested roles
- Marcus: lead on technical Q&A and perf benchmarks; have prepared logplots and latency-percentile slides (I attached the short perf deck in Drive).
- Laura: lead commercial and procurement discussion; draft concession/discount options and timeline to present.
- Rishi: be ready to field security-specific questions (SOC2, encryption, data residency).

Prep checklist for tomorrow’s internal sync (30 min):
1) Marcus to validate the Dedicated throughput numbers for GridLytics’ expected peak (see MAPP sheet).
2) Laura to prepare a proposed 12-month commitment tiers and quick ROI table.
3) Rishi to review Redwood_Prelim_Security_Checklist and pick 3 items to escalate if GridLytics requests deeper evidence.

I’ll take meeting logistics and the one-page exec summary. Quick internal sync 11:00 PDT today? If that works, I’ll send calendar.

-Neha

Alex — thanks, all good to proceed. We’ve put together the one-page exec summary (below) and two proposed slots. Please confirm which attendees will join and I’ll send the official calendar and pre-reads.

One-page exec summary (text)
- Ask: 45–60 minute steering committee to confirm security posture and procurement path for a Q3 pilot.
- What Redwood brings: predictable Dedicated capacity, automated fallback to hosted, built-in KV caching to reduce token costs, and SLO-backed latency targets.
- Key gating items: SOC2 evidence or equivalent, AUP around data retention (we propose 90-day default KV cache retention unless you require longer), and procurement signoff on committed tiers.

Proposed final slots (PDT):
- Wed Mar 11, 14:00–15:00 (preferred)
- Fri Mar 13, 09:00–10:00 (backup)

Requested attendees from GridLytics:
- CTO (or delegate)
